$comment: Arkchemy public progress data. Consumed by the woodburrow website. Standing rule: no category may ever exceed 95 -- there can always be bugs and issues later, so nothing is ever reported as finished.
generated_by: progress pass after class registration completed at 965 and the engine opened bootstrap.bld
max_percent_reason: Nothing is ever shown as 100%. Coverage is not correctness, and a category that looks finished can still be hiding bugs.

overall.headline: Class registration is complete. All 965 classes the retail game registers during boot now register here, in the retail order, and the engine has opened its own data files for the first time.
overall.summary: Seven silent bugs have been found and fixed, the largest being that only .rela.text was ever read, leaving 48,625 pointers stored in data null. Two more fell on 2026-08-30. The singleton descriptor list was closing into a ring because static initializers ran twice -- the harness walks the constructor table and the game's own GHS runtime walks it again -- so one traversal visited 38,154 nodes instead of five; guarding each initializer to run once fixed it and took bucket allocations from 18 to retail's exact 3. Then a job-queue spin turned out to be an ABI error: PPC EABI passes 64-bit arguments in register pairs starting on an ODD register, and every Atomic64 shim read one register short, so a compare-and-swap could never match. With both fixed, registration went 124 to 157 to 722 to 965 -- the exact line count of the retail Cemu capture -- and igArkCore::init reached the file loading it exists to start, opening bootstrap.bld after the engine's own bootstrap.arc miss. The boot now stalls waiting in the job queue rather than failing: jqWorkerSleep polls OSWaitEventWithTimeout steadily with no allocations for 2.2 million calls. Whether the queue has idle workers or no workers at all is the open question, and the instrumented build that answers it has not yet been run on hardware. The larger half of the project is still untouched: proving 19,623 translated functions correct, and a GX2-to-deko3d shader pipeline that does not exist yet.

status.note: Registration completed on 2026-08-30 across eight hardware builds. A symbolized, unstripped Wii U build of a later game on the same engine was obtained on 2026-09-01, giving names for engine internals that have until now only been reachable by probe.

current_work.title: The job queue waits, and nothing arrives
current_work.detail: From frame 9,180 the boot runs at a steady 8,260 calls and 146,000 imports per 60 frames and nothing else happens -- no further file opens, no further registrations, and no allocations at all for 2.2 million calls. The imports are jqWorkerSleep calling OSWaitEventWithTimeout. Polling at that rate reads identically whether the queue has idle workers or no workers were ever created, and those need completely different fixes, so the next build simply counts threads created and started. One real defect was found while looking: the Cafe OS atomics were unsynchronised read-modify-writes, which stopped being safe once OSResumeThread began calling pthread_create and guest threads became real host threads sharing one address space. Fixed, but not yet shown to be the stall.
current_work.blocked_on: a hardware run of the 2026-08-30 17:59 build

next_work.title: Run the thread-counter build
next_work.detail: 176,420,217 bytes, links clean, test-seconds.txt on the card set to 420. It reports threads created and started, which separates an empty worker pool from an idle one. Nothing else can be concluded until it runs.

next_work.title: Read the job queue by name instead of by probe
next_work.detail: The symbolized Imaginators ELF names the whole module -- jqInit, jqWorkerThread, jqEnableWorkers, jqWorkersMask, jqGetNumWorkers -- for the same engine built by the same studio five years later. It is a strong guide to what worker startup requires, though any offset taken from it stays a hypothesis until confirmed against the actual target, which is a different build.

next_work.title: Code and data in one address space
next_work.detail: Functions use real addresses and data a synthetic one. Mapping .text real fixed the module-range test; extending it to data broke the boot and was reverted, and why it collides is still unknown.

projects.name: Conquertron
projects.role: PowerPC32 to C static recompiler core
projects.summary: PowerPC32 to C static recompiler. 100% of .text translates. Five silent codegen bugs found and fixed, the largest being that only .rela.text was ever read -- 48,625 relocations targeting .rodata and .data were discarded, leaving every pointer stored in data null.

categories.label: Translation coverage
categories.note: Every instruction in the target binary decodes and the whole thing links. Held at 95 rather than 100 on the standing rule -- coverage is not a claim that any of it is right.

categories.label: Verified correctness
categories.note: Most translated functions have never been exercised by a real run. Unverified, not confirmed good. verify.sh covers arithmetic, floats, globals, function pointers, rodata tables and stripped-binary boundary recovery against ground truth on host and ARM64. Import-call instrumentation now emits from codegen, so a regenerated tree can tell a live shim loop from a genuine hang -- a distinction no existing counter could make.

categories.label: Relocation and addressing
categories.note: LWZU and ADDIC relocation-fold bugs found and fixed; RA=0 base-register handling fixed. Data-side .rodata mapping is the remaining open question.

projects.name: Jouster
projects.role: Switch runtime, Cafe OS shim layer, and the homebrew .nro itself
projects.summary: The Switch side. Class registration is complete at 965 of 965 in the retail order, and igArkCore::init has reached file loading and opened the engine's own bootstrap.bld. Real decoded video frames reach the panel from the game's own movie files with no shader translation in the path, and the Wii U boot splash and jingle play from meta/. The boot now waits in the job queue rather than failing.

categories.label: Cafe OS shim layer
categories.note: coreinit memory, filesystem, threading and synchronisation shims are real and working. The 64-bit atomics were corrected twice on 2026-08-30: their argument registers were one short of the PPC EABI odd-register pairing, and they were unsynchronised read-modify-writes on memory that real host threads now share. nsyshid and vpad are wired. gx2 is present and linkable but the shader and draw-call family are deliberate no-ops. Video is no longer a no-op: the game's own Bink API is served natively and delivers every luma row of each frame.

categories.label: Engine bring-up
categories.note: Up from 55. Registration reaches 965 of 965 classes in exactly the retail order -- the exact line count of the Cemu capture -- and the engine is past it, into the file loading igArkCore::init exists to start. bootstrap.arc misses and bootstrap.bld opens, which is the engine's own fallback order, not an error. Remaining blocker is a wait in the job queue.

categories.label: Graphics (GX2 to deko3d)
categories.note: gx2_test is real, working infrastructure -- render state, surfaces, buffers, texture binding, clear and present, VSync, GPU submission, all validated. What does not exist: a model or mesh loader, a material path, and any shader translation. GX2 shaders are compiled AMD R600 machine code; deko3d wants offline-compiled Nvidia Maxwell binaries. There is no runtime translation path, and building one is a substantial project in its own right.

categories.label: Figure reading (portal, dumps, Joy-Con NFC)
categories.note: skylanders_figure.c and skylanders_mifare_keys.c are compiled and passing on the host -- MIFARE Key A derivation matches all 80 known-good test vectors. skylanders_portal.c (USB HID) and skylanders_nfc.c (Joy-Con) need libnx and real hardware and are entirely unverified. No character select UI yet.

projects.name: Blaster
projects.role: Python tooling and host-testable regression tests
projects.summary: The tools that do not need a Switch. igz_tools.py handles Alchemy IGZ archives, extract_field_schema.py statically recovered 616 field names across 616 engine classes with no running game, the Wii to Wii U voice-line transplant pipeline swapped 1,481 English lines across 76 archives, and verify.sh is the recompiler's own correctness suite. verify.sh could not run from a clean clone until 2026-08-23 -- it still referenced the pre-split monorepo layout.

categories.label: IGZ and archive tooling
categories.note: Read paths are solid. No write path yet -- and a known trap waiting for one: omitting a memory-pool category when re-saving an igz silently misroutes data rather than failing.

categories.label: Recompiler correctness suite
categories.note: 18 harnesses run against ground truth on host and under QEMU ARM64, plus a stripped-binary boundary-recovery check. Four harness files at the repo root are not wired into verify.sh at all.

categories.label: Field schema extraction
categories.note: Field names recover statically. Byte offsets are computed at runtime and need a live hook into a running game -- NefariousTechSupport's AlchemyMetadataDumper is the closest existing prior art and already has a TARGET_CAFE guard defined.

projects.name: Woodburrow
projects.summary: Deliberately stripped back to a skeleton on 2026-08-22 so the design could be rebuilt by hand. What works today: the contributor cards (a hand-made HUD design, element symbols, battle classes) and the org repository list, both fed from live data. Every visitor lookup goes through this site's own serverless routes rather than the visitor's browser talking to GitHub or Discord directly.

categories.label: Contributors and credits
categories.note: Live from CONTRIBUTORS.csv, with element symbols, battle classes, avatars and a Special Thanks section.

categories.label: Serverless proxy routes
categories.note: Four routes keep visitor IPs off third-party logs and share one edge-cached lookup instead of each browser burning its own rate limit. One hardening gap is open in the image proxy -- see the security notes.

categories.label: Public pages (progress, findings, about, licence)
categories.note: Not rebuilt yet after the strip-down. This file and findings.json are the data those pages need.

projects.name: Armory
projects.role: Skylanders Online locker and account linking
projects.summary: Created and scaffolded on 2026-08-22 with the shared codenames and contributor files, plus its own stricter licence. Nothing is implemented. The locker is a Switch .nro, not a website feature; account linking is the website half. Both are blocked behind rendering and audio working at all, so this is deliberately parked rather than stalled.

categories.label: On-device locker
categories.note: Blocked on GX2 model rendering and audio playback. Useful lead found in the Discord exports: the figure-summon sequence ('Magic Moment' is the real in-engine term) is implemented in tfbscript, in game data, not hardcoded in the executable -- so the presentation logic may already exist natively rather than needing to be written.

timeline.milestone: Video from the game's own files displaying on hardware -- reached 2026-08-29, partially: frames decode and display, but truncate after a few macroblock rows.
timeline.estimate_fast: about 18 months from the start, so roughly early 2028
timeline.basis: Solo, part-time effort around college. Phase 1 (recompiler) and Phase 2 (GX2 and shaders) are each comparable in scope, and Phase 2 has barely started. Comparable public projects -- N64: Recompiled, Zelda 64: Recompiled -- took multiple contributors several years and had existing decompilation work to build on. This one does not.
timeline.caveat: The cutscene is a late-stage milestone, not an early one. It needs most of the pipeline working, not just booting.

stages.stage: Phase 1 against the real binary, executing without crashing
Phase 2 minimum viable GX2 and shader rendering
Phase 2a video and audio codec work
Debugging and integration for this specific cutscene

games.title: Swap Force

games.title: Trap Team
games.why: The third distinct porting studio. Resolve every known authorship lineage while still in toolchain-building mode.

games.title: Giants
games.why: First cheap confirmation pass, and by far the easiest of the six to obtain legally.

games.title: Imaginators
games.why: Last -- most content-divergent and the latest engine build, so it gets the most mature toolchain.
